RA 9492 (2007) restated Section 26: holidays move to the nearest Monday, and Ninoy Aquino Day and Eidul Fitr are listed. Earlier, RA 9177 (2002) had added Eidul Fitr as a national holiday and Eidul Adha as a regional holiday in the ARMM, and RA 9256 (2004) had declared August 21 Ninoy Aquino Day.

RA 9849 (2009) restated Section 26 again and made Eidul Adha a national holiday. The proviso on movable holidays reads as LawPhil transcribes it; RA 9492’s version reads “the President shall issue a proclamation, at least six months prior to the holiday concerned, the specific date that shall be declared as a nonworking day”. Check the Official Gazette text before relying on the exact words.

Later laws add special days without rewriting Section 26: July 27, founding anniversary of the Iglesia ni Cristo, a special national working holiday (RA 9645, 2009); December 8, Feast of the Immaculate Conception, a special nonworking holiday (RA 10966, 2017). Other dates each year (for example Chinese New Year, EDSA anniversary, All Souls’ Day) are set by presidential proclamation.

RA 8524 (1998) made the term of barangay officials and sangguniang kabataan members five years. It was later superseded: RA 9164 (2002) set three years, and RA 12232 (2025) now sets four (below).

RA 9244 (2004) eliminated the preparatory recall assembly: recall is now initiated only by a petition of registered voters, with graduated signature thresholds based on the voting population, verified by the COMELEC.

RA 9640 (2009) lowered the maximum provincial amusement tax from thirty to ten percent of gross receipts from admission fees, and added that the proceeds are shared equally by the province and the municipality where the amusement places are located.
RA 9009 (2001) raised the income requirement for conversion into a component city from ₱20 million to ₱100 million (at 2000 constant prices), locally generated, for two consecutive years.

RA 11683 (2022) is the text in force. It keeps the ₱100 million income requirement (2000 constant prices) with either 100 square kilometers of territory or 150,000 inhabitants, and adds a second route: a locally generated average annual income of at least ₱400 million (2012 constant prices) with a population or territorial requirement, the ₱400 million threshold rising by five percent every three years. New paragraph (d) lets a converted city keep its municipal share in the national taxes for three years. Two passages are garbled in the transcription — the repeated “territory of at least” in (a)(i), and the population figure of the second route, which is missing (“not less than one by the PSA”) — check the official text.

RA 8185 (1996) rewrote paragraph (d): the five-percent calamity fund may be used for relief, rehabilitation, reconstruction and other calamity works, only in the area affected as declared by the sanggunian. The legal rate of interest is six percent a year from July 1, 2013 (BSP Monetary Board Circular No. 799). Nacar v. Gallery Frames (2013) sets the rules on when it runs, including six percent on a final money judgment until satisfied.

Interest ceilings under the Usury Law were suspended by Central Bank Circular No. 905 (1982), so parties may agree on interest; but courts strike down rates that are iniquitous or unconscionable (Medel v. Court of Appeals, 1998).

Judicial confirmation now needs at least twenty years of open, continuous, exclusive and notorious possession of alienable and disposable land immediately before filing, instead of possession since June 12, 1945 or earlier; it caps the area at twelve hectares and lets the application be filed “at any time”. Its Section 7 makes a DENR geodetic engineer’s certification on the survey plan sufficient proof that the land is alienable and disposable.
